definitions.explanation: The elected head of a prefectural government in Japan. Each of Japan's 47 prefectures has one governor.

examples.japanese: {知事|ちじ}{選挙|せんきょ}は{来月|らいげつ}だ。
examples.english: The gubernatorial election is next month.

examples.japanese: {東京都|とうきょうと}{知事|ちじ}が{会見|かいけん}を{開|ひら}いた。
examples.english: The Governor of Tokyo held a press conference.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{知事|ちじ}は{若|わか}い{女性|じょせい}だ。
examples.english: The new governor is a young woman.

examples.japanese: {知事|ちじ}が{防災|ぼうさい}{訓練|くんれん}に{参加|さんか}した。
examples.english: The governor participated in disaster preparedness training.

examples.japanese: {県|けん}{知事|ちじ}に{立候補|りっこうほ}する{人|ひと}が{三人|さんにん}いる。
examples.english: There are three candidates running for prefectural governor.

notes:
{知事|ちじ} is the elected head of a {都道府県|とどうふけん} (prefecture). Japan has 47 prefectures, each with its own {知事|ちじ}.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- 〜{県|けん}{知事|ちじ}: governor of ~ Prefecture
- {知事|ちじ}{選挙|せんきょ}: gubernatorial election
- {知事|ちじ}に{当選|とうせん}する: to be elected governor
- {知事|ちじ}に{立候補|りっこうほ}する: to run for governor

RELATED TITLES:
- {市長|しちょう}: mayor (city)
- {町長|ちょうちょう}: mayor (town)
- {村長|そんちょう}: village chief
- {総理大臣|そうりだいじん}: prime minister

NOTE:
The titles vary by prefecture type: {東京都|とうきょうと}{知事|ちじ}, {大阪府|おおさかふ}{知事|ちじ}, {北海道|ほっかいどう}{知事|ちじ}, 〜{県|けん}{知事|ちじ}.
